# `@telnyx/edge-runtime`

Runtime SDK for Telnyx Edge Compute.

## Actor-to-actor calls (`this.env`)

Inside a `StatefulActor`, `this.env` carries one namespace per `[[actors]]`
binding declared in your `telnyx.toml`, so an actor can call another actor
(the substrate for agents spawning sub-agents):

```ts
class Concierge extends StatefulActor {
  async delegate() {
    // env.<BINDING>.idFromName(id).<method>(...args)
    return this.env.ROLODEX.idFromName("shared").remember("caller", this.ctx.id);
  }
}
```

Calls go to the actor-invocation base URL — the local Dapr sidecar by default,
or the site actor router when `EC_ACTOR_ROUTER_URL` is set; the callee's turn
runs (and its state persists) exactly as a direct invocation would.

> **Self-call hazard (no re-entrancy).** An actor is single-threaded **per id** —
> like a Cloudflare Durable Object. Calling **your own id** from inside a method
> (`this.env.<BINDING>.idFromName(this.ctx.id).m()`) **deadlocks**: the nested
> call queues behind the turn you're already in, so it can't run until you return
> — and you can't return until it does. It rejects with `ActorMethodTimeoutError`
> once the method wall-clock budget elapses. Calling a **different** id (even of
> the same type) is fine — the turn lock is per `(type, id)`.
